name: Matya Samo
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Berthelette 2002 SIL survey report on San (Samo) located; sociolinguistic, no phonology/stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages maty1235 / mand1437 and local Glottolog bibliography dump ( /): 7 refs for maty1235 (Boro 1986; Tauxier 1917; Morse 1967; Berthelette 2001; ISO CR 2012-140; Prost 1953 Vocabulaires compares; Ebermann 2009).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; alt names for maty1235 include 'Tougan', confirming Boro 1986 belongs here.

sources.citation: Perekhvalskaya, Elena. 2017. Basic morphosyntax of verbal and non-verbal clauses in San-Maka. Mandenkan 57: 49-76. doi:10.4000/mandenkan.1070 (SIBLING: Southern Samo, sout2844, Toma variety).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.2 para 24: 'San-Maka is a tonal language with three level tones, designated, according to IPA, by acute, macron and gravis diacritics. Tones in San-Maka play a role in both the lexicon and grammar.' No mention of stress/accent. Sec. 1 surveys the cluster (Maka/Makya=Matya/Maya), cites an unpublished SIL 'Guide d'orthographe san macaa' for the Matya variety and Ebermann's four northern lects.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Samo language (Burkina)'; Ethnologue 2016 page for stj via the Internet Archive (location Sourou/Kossi, alt names Northwestern Samo, Sane, Tougan).
sources.note: Nothing on tone or stress; used only for dialect geography/identity.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-140 (Erwin Ebermann & Henning Schreiber): split stj Samo, Matya into Sane Central / North-Western / Southern (rejected 2013-05-20); main form + new-code forms sfc, sfd, sfn.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; states Ebermann collected 'lexical data, tonology, phonology, morphology, syntax' in 12 settlements of all four Sane regions (unpublished); places Tougan, Kouy, Kassoum in 'Central Sane' (Matya); bibliography lists Boro 1986, Ebermann 1990, 1991, 2009.

sources.citation: [SIL / ANTBA, sous-commission de la langue san mayaa]. 2011. Guide d'orthographe san mayaa, edition preliminaire (juin 2011), with Lexique san mayaa. 81 pp. (SIBLING: Maya Samo, maya1279, Bangassogo standard).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.4 'Le ton' (p. 9): 'Bien que le ton joue un role important dans la prononciation san, [les mots qui] ne se distingue[nt] que par la melodie tonale sont assez rares', so tone is written (acute accent) on only six words. Nothing on stress; 'accent' is used only for the diacritic.

sources.citation: Berthelette, John. 2001 [SIL ESR 2002-005, 2002]. Survey report on the San (Samo) language. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-005. Dallas: SIL International. 75 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: sociolinguistic/intelligibility survey with a wordlist appendix; the words tone, tonal, stress, accent do not occur. Sec. 1.9 and the bibliography identify the phonological descriptions: Boro 1986 (Tougan = Matya), Ki 1985 (Toma), Platiel 1974 (Toma); defines matya region = NW, west and north of Tougan (Kassoum, Kouy, Toeni).

sources.citation: Ebermann, Erwin. Publication list / CV, homepage.univie.ac.at/erwin.ebermann/publ.htm (lists 1990 'Possessivrelationen im Nordsamo' AAP 24: 53-67; 1991 'Genitivverbindungen in den noerdlichen Samo-Sprachen' Afrika und Uebersee 74: 67-76; 2009 negation chapter; talks 'Die Tonologie des Nordsamo' (18. Afrikanistentag, Wien 2007) and 'Dialectology and Language Contact in the Northern Samo Region' (Mande congress, St Petersburg 2008)).
sources.note: Nothing quotable; establishes that a tonology of Northern Samo exists only as an unpublished 2007 conference talk; no downloads offered.

sources.citation: Ebermann, Erwin. 2009. From double negation to portmanteau: comparative sentence negation in Northern Samo. In Norbert Cyffer, Erwin Ebermann & Georg Ziegelmeyer (eds.), Negation Patterns in West African Languages and Beyond (TSL 87), 119-152. Amsterdam/Philadelphia: John Benjamins.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Most recent published linguistic treatment of the northern Samo lects (Maya base, Matya compared) by the only linguist with tonological field data on them; expected to contain a phonology/tone preamble and tone-marked data.

sources.citation: SIL Burkina Faso / ANTBA. n.d. [c. 2011]. Guide d'orthographe san macaa. Edition preliminaire (with Lexique san macaa and text sample). Ouagadougou: SIL. (unpublished; cited by Perekhvalskaya 2017: 34)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Matya-specific orthography statement by the SIL San Macaa team; its sister volume for Mayaa has a section 'Le ton', so this one almost certainly states the tone/stress facts for Matya.

sources.citation: Ebermann, Erwin. 2007. Die Tonologie des Nordsamo. Paper read at the 18. Afrikanistentag, Wien, 23-25 July 2007 (unpublished; handout/slides) — together with Ebermann 1990 'Possessivrelationen im Nordsamo', Afrikanistische Arbeitspapiere 24: 53-67 and 1991 'Genitivverbindungen in den noerdlichen Samo-Sprachen', Afrika und Uebersee 74: 67-76.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only dedicated tonology of Northern Samo (incl. Matya lects); would state directly whether there is any word stress beside tone. The 1990/1991 articles may carry a transcription note on tone/accent.

sources.citation: Boro, J. M. 1986. Elements de phonologie sani, parler de Tougan (Burkina Faso). Memoire de maitrise. Ouagadougou: Universite de Ouagadougou, IN.SU.L.L.A.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only phonological description of the Matya (Tougan) variety itself (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a phonology); a prosody/tone chapter would settle the stress question first-hand.

sources.citation: Platiel, Suzanne. 1974. Description du parler samo de Toma (Haute-Volta): phonologie, syntaxe. These de doctorat d'Etat, Universite Paris V. 642 pp. (also Platiel 1987-88, 'A propos du systeme vocalique en san', Mandenkan 14-15: 251-264)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The foundational San phonology (Southern variety) with a dialect survey of the matya/maya north (pp. 18-25); its prosody chapter is the reference statement for the cluster and would show whether any San variety has been described with stress.

sources.citation: Prost, Andre. 1953. Les langues mande-sud du groupe mana-busa. Memoires de l'IFAN 26. Dakar: IFAN. (samo sketch + 'Vocabulaires compares' pp. 77-182)
